subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw change startup SecretRef resolution from immediate fail-fast to a bounded retry/degrade policy for side-effecting exec providers, and if so what behavior is allowed by default?
rationale: The observable issue is real, but changing startup secret behavior affects security posture, supervisor recovery, credential-provider load, and whether users get an explicit startup failure or a delayed/degraded service.

options.title: Define Generic Startup Policy
options.body: Approve a provider-agnostic bounded retry/degrade design with clear logs, tests, and docs, then allow a focused fix against `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` and `src/secrets/resolve.ts`.

options.title: Keep Fail-Fast, Improve Guidance
options.body: Preserve the current fail-fast startup contract and document supervisor restart limits plus plugin-backed caching/batching resolvers for quota-sensitive providers.

options.title: Add Configurable Retry Surface
options.body: Sponsor a new explicit retry/backoff config contract with schema/docs/tests, accepting the compatibility cost of a new operator-facing configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Define Generic Startup Policy
recommendation.body: Approve a provider-agnostic bounded retry/degrade design with clear logs, tests, and docs, then allow a focused fix against `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` and `src/secrets/resolve.ts`.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest feature-history signal for the SecretRef resolver/runtime contract whose startup policy needs owner judgment.
